claims.text: A predictive approach incorporating local lattice distortion, atomic mass variance, and vibrational anharmonicity will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than average-property models.
Local lattice distortion, atomic mass variance, and vibrational anharmonicity are quantitative descriptors of configurational disorder relevant to phonon transport.
The intended materials are equiatomic or near-equiatomic HEAs with high configurational disorder and single-phase or nearly single-phase structures without significant segregation.
The advanced method will be used to screen a broad HEA candidate set and select alloys predicted to have enhanced phonon scattering.
Room-temperature and elevated-temperature measurements are representative of thermal-insulation applications.
Applicability requires thermodynamically stable, single-phase alloys.
Applicability requires conventional phonon-transport regimes in which electronic heat conduction is not dominant.
Local lattice distortions and atomic-mass disorder enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces phonon mean free path.
Explicit disorder and anharmonicity descriptors capture phonon-scattering mechanisms more effectively than averaged material properties.
Improved representation of scattering mechanisms will produce more accurate forecasts of very low phonon thermal conductivity.
Selected HEAs will have measured phonon thermal conductivity at least approximately 20% below values predicted by conventional approaches.
Selected HEAs will have lower phonon thermal conductivity than HEAs selected without the refined descriptors.
Conventional prediction methods average material properties and omit local disorder-driven anharmonic phonon scattering.
The approach will be less effective or inapplicable in HEAs with marked phase separation.
The approach will be less effective or inapplicable when electronic heat conduction dominates.
The exact improvement and compositional applicability boundaries are uncertain pending experimental validation.
Laser-flash analysis and time-domain thermoreflectance will be used to determine thermal transport in synthesized candidates.
Failure to obtain at least a 20% reduction relative to conventional predictions, or performance similar to standard-method selections, will falsify the claimed superiority.
